text.p: Italian state engineering company Finmeccanica said it was negotiating a medium to long term debt facility for 3.0 trillion lire which would repay a similar amount of short term debt.
Finmeccanica said in a statement in response to an Italian press report it was negotiating "a revolving medium and long term financial operation likely to be for 3.0 trillion" on the domestic market.

Financial daily Milano Finanza said the group's creditor banks had been asked to switch a good part of their short term exposure to the medium and long term with a seven year 3.0 trillion credit facility at a rate based on three-month Ribor.
The report said the facility would equal 80 percent of the short term exposure of the 30 creditor banks which stood at 3.75 trillion on September 30.
The banks were expected to reply by January 22, 1997.

Finmeccanica said within the framework of a rescheduling of its debt towards the medium and long term, in the last two years it had carried out financial operations on foreign markets totalling over 1.5 trillion lire.
Finmeccanica said at the end of November it expected to reduce group net financial debt to 5.4 trillion lire by the end of 1996 from 5.98 trillion reported at the end of June.
The company is Italy's largest defence and aerospace group and is controlled by state industrial holding Iri.
